t: An Ottoman officer from Salonica who rose to prominence at Gallipoli, Mustafa Kemal led the Turkish National Movement against the partition of the country after the First World War and won a victory confirmed in the Treaty of Lausanne of 1923.

As first president of the Republic of Turkey from 1923 to 1938 he abolished the caliphate, closed the religious courts and orders, introduced a secular civil code and the Latin-based alphabet, and gave women equal civil and political rights.

He ruled a one-party state that suppressed its opponents and pressed minorities such as the Kurds to assimilate; praised as a nation-builder and an inspiration to anti-colonial movements, he is also condemned for repression and for continuing the persecution of Christian minorities begun by the CUP.
dyk: When Mustafa Kemal asked linguists in 1928 how long a new Latin-based alphabet would take to introduce, most said three to five years; he is said to have answered, "We shall do it in three to five months." The alphabet was introduced on 1 November 1928.
ev: Born Mustafa in Salonica, in the Ottoman Empire, to Ali Rıza Efendi and Zübeyde Hanım
The Ottoman Empire enters the First World War, a step he thought a fatal mistake; at Gallipoli he commands the 19th Division and holds his position until the Allies retreat
Lands at Samsun on 19 May to organise a national movement against the occupation and issues the Amasya Circular
As commander in chief defeats the Greek army at the Battle of the Sakarya and is made field marshal and Gazi
The Treaty of Lausanne is signed and the Republic of Turkey is proclaimed, with him as its first president
The caliphate is abolished and its powers transferred to the Grand National Assembly; sharia courts are closed
Introduces the Latin-based Turkish alphabet and abolishes the use of the Arabic script
Dies of cirrhosis at Dolmabahçe Palace in Istanbul and is succeeded by İsmet İnönü

f.born: c. 1881 in Salonica (Selanik), Ottoman Empire, as Mustafa; son of Ali Rıza Efendi, a military officer, title deed clerk and lumber trader, and Zübeyde Hanım; a Muslim, Turkish-speaking family that Andrew Mango calls precariously middle-class
f.died: 10 November 1938 at Dolmabahçe Palace in Istanbul, aged 57, of cirrhosis; laid to rest in the Ethnography Museum of Ankara and moved to the mausoleum of Anıtkabir in 1953
f.role: Ottoman army officer (from 1905); commander of the 19th Division at Gallipoli; leader of the Turkish National Movement and speaker of the Grand National Assembly (from 1920); commander in chief (1921), field marshal and Gazi; founder of the People's Party (1923); first president of the Republic of Turkey (1923–1938)
f.known: the Defence of Gallipoli; the Turkish War of Independence; founding the Republic of Turkey (1923); abolishing the sultanate and the caliphate; the Latin-based Turkish alphabet (1928); equal civil and political rights for women; Kemalism and its Six Arrows; the one-party state and Turkification
